review.brief:
Review RM35-app-adopt-clock (roadmap RM35 tier 5, module internal/app) against the DIFF, not the whole module. Validate:
(1) Module-boundary compliance per ai/architecture.md — app composes modules through public interfaces; internal/clock added to its May-import list.
(2) The one real behaviour change: NewScheduler's nil-loc fallback moves time.Local -> clock.Zone(). Confirm no doc comment, AGENTS.md line or test name still describes the old time.Local behaviour as current.
(3) The critical non-change: recalculateAnalytics must still pass p.loc — the poller's own configured zone — to clock.CalendarDay, NOT clock.Zone(). Substituting the platform default would change day attribution and contradicts RM29 design D-B12. Verify the delegation is algebraically identical for every input.
(4) Roadmap D6 — no NEW tests added; exactly one existing test repaired (the nil-loc fallback assertion), every other expected value UNCHANGED. A moved expected value elsewhere is a blocker.
(5) design.md's Test Contract was authored up front — check the repaired test asserts what design.md specifies.
(6) Doc-pack conventions: ai/go-conventions.md timezone rule (no raw time.Now(), no hardcoded zone name outside clock); CLAUDE.md's docs-track-structural-change.
(7) Performance-Profile compliance (read-heavy).
(8) No database object created or changed. Any schema touch is a blocker.
(9) Anti-gaming: no task title, criterion or expected value weakened.
Test provenance: go build ./... , go vet ./... and gofmt were ASSISTANT-run. The suite (go test ./internal/app/... and go test ./...) was run and reported passing by the OWNER. Judge test QUALITY by reading them; do not run the suite yourself.

decisions.decision: recalculateAnalytics keeps passing p.loc — the poller's configured zone — to clock.CalendarDay, rather than clock.Zone().
decisions.why: RM29 design D-B12 makes this composition, not internal/analytics, the owner of which day is being asked about. Substituting the platform default would change day attribution.
